text: Vectors. Scalers and vectors. What is a scalar? A scalar defines the amount of something in one dimension. They are accompanied by a unit which signifies the dimension in particular. We learn about dimensions as a concept of length, for example meters, but a dimension can be generally described as one aspect of a thing. For example, your car, see the figure on the course webpage, has multiple dimensions, mass, 1500 kilograms, age, four year, gas tank, 10 gal, gas mileage, 40 MPG. Each of these dimensions for describing the car has a number followed by the unit which makes up the scalar quantity. Scalar arithmetic. Scalar quantities can only be combined or separated when they have the same unit. For example, a 50 minute class that ends 10 minute early lasts for 50 minute minus 10 minute equals 40 minute. If you were told that the class ended 600 seconds early, you cannot combine or separate the quantities directly. Instead, you must first convert to a common unit then you can proceed as before. 50 minute minus 600 seconds equals 50 minute minus 600 seconds over 1 times 1 minute over 60 seconds equals 50 minute minus 10 minute equals 40 minute. Note, you can write in math mode using dollar sign pairs or using the align environment given as backslash begin, brace, align, brace, backslash end, brace, align, brace. The Python example is available on the course webpage. Scalers can also be multiplied and divided where units can be combined under the appropriate operation. For example, energy is described by the amount of force applied that is multiplied over a distance or E equals FD. Suppose you pushed a 0.5 kilogram box with a force of 1 Newton horizontally across the floor for 5 meters. See the figure on the course webpage. Then you expended 5 Newton meters of energy. The unit is combined to form a Newton meter or jewel. If you traveled to Dallas from commerce, approximately 60 miles away, in your car, and the trip took one hour, then your average speed is a derived scalar quantity of 60 miles per hour. Checkpoint, pause and check your understanding. A class lasts 50 minutes, but ends 600 seconds early. Can you subtract these quantities immediately or must you convert units first? What is a vector? A vector combines scalar quantities as a new object that delineates the quantities by their dimension. A unit vector represents a single step along a dimensional axis and is signified using the hat symbol over the variable for that axis. For example, one unit step along the x-axis is represented by x-hat, which can be written in Markdown syntax as dollar sign, backslash, hat, brace, x- brace, dollar sign, in a text cell in your Jupyter notebook. Consider a chessboard where players designate letters and numbers to identify a piece at a particular location on the board. The chess pieces move as vectors to traverse the chessboard. The knight moves in an L-shaped pattern that can include moving the piece either one space horizontally, two spaces vertically, or two spaces horizontally, one space vertically. Both of these choices represent a vector when we consider the initial and final locations of the knight. The Python code is available on the course web page. A vector is also described as an object that has both magnitude and direction. See the figure on the course web page. Physical quantities specified by giving a number of units, e.g. magnitude and direction, e.g. angle or up, down, left, right, are called vector quantities. Examples include position, displacement, change in position, velocity, change in position per time, acceleration, change in velocity per time, force, torque. Vectors can be combined together to make a new vector or multiplied by a scalar to create a vector of a new length. The chessboard example above showed the resultant vector is composed by the addition of two component vectors. Vectors are distinguished from scalars using an arrow over the variable. Suppose we can identify the position vector of an object because it is two kilometers due east, then we can write the vector m equals two times x hat kilometers, where x hat represents the direction due east or along the positive x axis. The x hat is a unit vector with a length equal to one. Note, in your Jupyter Notebook Markdown Text Cell, vector m is represented by the Markdown Source Text, dollar sign, backslash, veck, brace, m, brace, dollar sign, and x hat is represented by the source text, dollar sign, backslash, hat, brace, x, brace, dollar sign. Be sure to use dollar sign pairs around your latex symbols so they render properly. The latex cheat sheet is linked on the course webpage. The object vector m is a vector because it has a magnitude, two kilometers, and a direction, x hat. The magnitude can be written equivalently as m equivalent to the magnitude of vector m. What is the vector for an object that is two kilometers due west? What is the vector for an object that is two kilometers due north south? Note that we have chosen the x in x hat arbitrarily, where we could have used any other symbol. You might see that other textbooks use i hat instead. The problem, a long measuring stick rests against a wall in a physics laboratory with its 200 centimeter end at the floor. A Ladybug lands at the 100 centimeter mark and crawls randomly along the stick. It first walks 15 centimeters toward the floor, then it walks 56 centimeters toward the wall, then it walks 3 centimeters toward the floor again. Then after a brief stop, it continues 25 centimeters toward the floor, and then again it crawls 19 centimeters toward the wall before coming to a complete rest. Find the vector of the total displacement and its final resting position on the stick. The model. We model the Ladybug's motion as one-dimensional motion along the length of the measuring stick. The stick defines a single axis, so each part of the motion is either in the positive direction or the negative direction along that axis. We choose the direction toward the floor as positive and represent that direction with the unit vector U hat. The motion toward the wall is therefore in the negative U hat direction. The net displacement is found by treating each crawl segment as a signed displacement along the same line. The math. The five displacement vectors are vector D1 equals 15 centimeters times plus U hat. Vector D2 equals 56 centimeters times minus U hat. Vector D3 equals 3 centimeters times plus U hat. Vector D4 equals 25 centimeters times plus U hat. Vector D5 equals 19 centimeters times minus U hat. The total displacement vector is vector D equals vector D1 plus vector D2 plus vector D3 plus vector D4 plus vector D5 equals 15 minus 56 plus 3 plus 25 minus 19 centimeters U hat equals negative 32 centimeters times U hat. The conclusion. The Ladybug's total displacement vector is vector D equals negative 32 centimeters U hat. The negative sign means the net displacement is toward the wall. Since the Ladybug started at the 100 centimeter mark, the final position is the 68 centimeter mark on the measuring stick. Algebra of vectors in 2D. Vectors can be oriented in any direction, not just parallel or anti-parallel. This complicates their addition, where you cannot simply add their magnitudes to determine the resultant vector. Instead, we must use geometry to construct the resultant vector and trigonometry to find vector magnitudes and directions. For a geometric construction of the sum of two vectors in a plane, we follow the parallelogram rule. The relevant figures are shown on the course webpage. To add two vectors, vector A plus vector B, we can construct a parallelogram by shifting each vector to a parallel copy so that we can trace a path from the origin to the opposite corner of the parallelogram. The subtraction of two vectors, vector A minus vector B, is performed in a similar way. However, notice a key difference. In vector addition, the second vector is translated without changing direction. In vector subtraction, the vector being subtracted is reversed first. The method of tail-to-head geometric construction can be generalized to combine multiple vectors together. Consider four vectors, vector A, vector B, vector C, and vector D, as shown on the course webpage. We can select any one of the vectors to start with because vector addition is commutative and associative where the resultant vector R equals vector A plus vector B plus vector C plus vector D. Starting with vector D, we make a parallel translation of a second vector A to a position where its tail coincides with the head of the first vector D, a third vector C to a position where its origin coincides with the end of vector A, and a fourth vector B to a position where its origin coincides with the end of vector C. We draw the resultant vector R by connecting the tail of the first vector D to the head of the last vector B. Checkpoint. Pause and check your understanding. Two vectors are drawn tail-to-head. Where should the resultant vector start and where should it end? The problem. The three displacement vectors, vector A, vector B, and vector C lie in the horizontal plane. Their magnitudes are A equals 10.0 centimeters, B equals 7.0 centimeters, and C equals 8.0 centimeters, respectively. And their direction angles measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis are alpha equals 35 degrees, beta equals negative 110 degrees, and gamma equals 30 degrees. Choose a convenient scale and use a ruler and a protractor to find the following vector sums. A, vector R equals vector A plus vector B. B, vector D equals vector A minus vector B. C, vector S equals vector A minus 3 vector B plus vector C. The figure is shown on the course webpage. The model. We model each displacement as a two-dimensional vector in the horizontal plane. Each vector has a magnitude and a direction angle measured relative to the positive x-axis. Because this is a geometric construction, the vectors are drawn to scale and placed either tail-to-head or tail-to-tail depending on the combination being represented. Vector subtraction is modeled by reversing the direction of the vector being subtracted while keeping its magnitude unchanged. The resultant is the single vector that represents the combined effect of the vectors in the diagram. The math. For a geometric construction, the magnitude and direction of each resultant are obtained by drawing the vectors to scale and then measuring the resultant vector. The direction angles are measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis. A, for the sum vector, R equals vector A plus vector B. The vectors are drawn tail-to-head so that the tail of vector B is placed at the head of vector A. The resultant vector, R, is drawn from the tail of vector A to the head of vector B. Measuring the scaled diagram gives, R is approximately equal to 5.8 centimeters. Theta R is approximately equal to 0 degrees. B, for the difference vector, D equals vector A minus vector B. The subtraction is treated as addition of the opposite vector. The vector negative vector B has the same magnitude as vector B, but points in the opposite direction. So the construction uses vector D equals vector A plus negative vector B. Measuring the scaled diagram gives, D is approximately equal to 16.2 centimeters. Theta D is approximately equal to 49.3 degrees. C, for the linear combination vector, S equals vector A minus 3 vector B plus vector C. The vector B is first scaled by a factor of 3 and reversed to represent negative 3 vector B. The vectors are then drawn tail-to-head and vector S is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the final vector. Measuring the scaled diagram gives, S is approximately equal to 36.9 centimeters. Theta S is approximately equal to 52.9 degrees. The conclusion, the geometric construction gives the resultant values, R is approximately equal to 5.8 centimeters. Theta R is approximately equal to 0 degrees. D is approximately equal to 16.2 centimeters. Theta D is approximately equal to 49.3 degrees. And S is approximately equal to 36.9 centimeters. Theta S is approximately equal to 52.9 degrees. These results show that the same vector operations can be represented geometrically by drawing vectors to scale. But the accuracy of the result depends on the precision of the construction.

not just parallel or anti-parallel. This complicates their addition, where you cannot simply
add their magnitudes to determine the resultant vector. Instead, we must use geometry to construct
the resultant vector and trigonometry to find vector magnitudes and directions. For a geometric
construction of the sum of two vectors in a plane, we follow the parallelogram rule. The relevant
figures are shown on the course webpage. To add two vectors, vector A plus vector B, we can
construct a parallelogram by shifting each vector to a parallel copy so that we can trace a path
from the origin to the opposite corner of the parallelogram. The subtraction of two vectors,
vector A minus vector B, is performed in a similar way. However, notice a key difference. In vector
addition, the second vector is translated without changing direction. In vector subtraction,
the vector being subtracted is reversed first. The method of tail-to-head geometric construction
can be generalized to combine multiple vectors together. Consider four vectors, vector A, vector B,
vector C, and vector D, as shown on the course webpage. We can select any one of the vectors to
start with because vector addition is commutative and associative where the resultant vector R equals
vector A plus vector B plus vector C plus vector D. Starting with vector D, we make a parallel
translation of a second vector A to a position where its tail coincides with the head of the first
vector D, a third vector C to a position where its origin coincides with the end of vector A,
and a fourth vector B to a position where its origin coincides with the end of vector C.
We draw the resultant vector R by connecting the tail of the first vector D to the head of the
last vector B. Checkpoint. Pause and check your understanding. Two vectors are drawn tail-to-head.
